summary:
# NOTES: *Through the Sun in an Airship* (John Mastin, 1909; single book)

## Front matter
- Epigraph: Churchill ("keep a passage fair and plain").
- Author: John Mastin, F.S.A. Scot., F.L.S., F.C.S., F.R.A.S., F.R.M.S., R.B.A. Other works: *Parasites of Insects*, *The True Analysis of Milk*, *Plate-Culture and Staining of Amœbæ*, *The Stolen Planet*, *The Immortal Light*.
- Publisher: Charles Griffin & Co., Ltd., Exeter St, Strand, London. Printed by Ballantyne & Co.
- Dedication: to Prof. Sir Hubert von Herkomer, by his former pupil. Written at Totley Brook near Sheffield, June 1909.
- Contents: 17 chapters (I–XVII).

## Ch I: The Story of the *Regina*
- Setting: picnic clearing in forest, "Garden of the Earth" near North Pole, river Pole. Ross Ainley and Gilbert Eastern (physicist) with airships.
- Gilbert discards a rotten capsule egg from manufacturer "Flatters". Eggs are pink paste in capsules. Ross makes milk from a pellet.
- Ross laments the matter-of-fact age. Cites Nordenskiöld (1878/79), Admiral Wrangell, Anjou Hedenström. Says life originated at North Pole. Old Age Pensions; working-class revolution.
- Ross: man upsets nature; birds flee airships. Gilbert defends present: guaranteed Government wages, self-supporting prisons, restitution to victims.
- Ross dislikes compressed food and salmon capsules. Gilbert calls him "Alexander" type.
- Dennis Oakland arrives. Electrical expert; tied with Ross in last year's electrical exam. Greeting = grasp on upper arm, biceps.
- Bona: second moon, appeared after increased gravity. Luna is the old moon. Scales-and-cycles argument; stained glass lost and rediscovered.
- Dennis owns *Regina*, from the novel *The Stolen Planet* by ancestor Jervis Meredith. Inventors: Meredith and Fraser Burnley.
- History: *Regina* first voyage to Sirius; brought a planetoid back, then sent it inside Jupiter's orbit. Later Burnley opened the shed door and touched the ladder under current, and was vaporised.
- Dying Jervis Meredith told son Dennis ("Denny") to keep the secret, and died before revealing it. Shed lightning shows; vessel is untouched.
- Attempts: blasting with rystosol; tunnelling; the vessel hangs in equilibrium with gravity. Dennis refuses Government aid, citing a warrant signed by King Edward VII.
- Ross and Gilbert agree to help. Meeting set for next day at Derwent.

## Ch II: The *Regina* Gives Up Her Secret
- Shed: steel shutter, glass walls, roof folds. Dennis's hammer vaporises within a foot of the hull. Zone of destruction is 12 inches.
- Dummy suit of sawdust vaporised when dropped from roof.
- Two years of study. Storm watching gives an idea. Hats thrown; they pass.
- Ross, Gilbert and Dennis enter the vessel and reach the safe. Key handed down through generations.
- Crowd breaks in. Richard Howett, town chief, announces their "deaths".
- Dennis and friends float the crowd (about 60–70 people) using gravity control, then restore them. Dennis's "Ye floating spirits" speech. Crowd vows forgiveness.
- Ship declared theirs. Twice-nightly burglaries. Government deputation refused; warrant upheld.

## Ch III: *Vox Populi*
- Banquet; sceptics. Solomon Magson, official with *caput inflatum*, floats up after a demonstration. "You cannot insist, you have no will."
- Steel bar de-atomised. Magson asks to join; refused.
- Satire on women's name-retention and marriage. Settled as "husband and wife".
- Preparations: "breezol" cubes; doctors and formulae; wood-pulp clothing. None of the three is married.
- Test flight: Regina rises, scares airships, returns, lights stretch to England. Government pamphlet.
- Ether-wave daily at 6 pm. Target: valley "Kidney" on Bona. Departure 13 June.
- Traffic chaos in Derwent; two lives lost in crush. Regina rises up a "shaft" of ships at dawn.
- Paper souvenir floats: "Good-bye! good luck. Keep an eye on us if possible. This is a souvenir of the Regina; may you be able to keep it!" Owner frames it under glass.

## Ch IV: *Muscæ Vomitoriæ*
- Bona landing. Gravity about 32 ft/s². Noiseless capsule revolvers.
- Golden grass, red-brown trees, flowers of all seasons, sweetbriar. Red sandstone cliffs.
- Bathe in sea; skin and hair solidify. Stream: water pair dyes them blue (Prussian blue). Blueness persists.
- Bonians (spirits of vegetation): two-finger forehead salute; "rods" of magnetic steel paralyse. Ross's vanity wounded.
- Bonians cure them with ointment and lotion; desquamation takes about two months.
- Bonians telepathise with all planets except Earth.
- Bonians tell them of a fire-proof grub from Jupiter: crater like a flat cross.
- Expert chosen: Godfrey Spenser (microscopist; crank electrician).

## Ch V: An Innocent Offender
- Mid-September. Godfrey joins; 19 Sept storm voyage.
- Godfrey burns hand on switch of reel. Ross scolds him.
- Gilbert: Jupiter opposition 15 Oct.
- Heat lecture: Rumford/Davy 1798–99; Davy 1812 "motion"; water anomaly at 40°F and 32°F; ice-water mixtures.
- Godfrey moved steering switch. Ship drifts to Luna, not Jupiter.
- Luna data: gravity 0.10 of Earth; diameter 2160 miles; Lunians aggressive.
- Luna facts: Tycho rays 2624 miles; Mare Crisium; Oceanus Procellarum.

## Ch VI: The Doomed Planet
- Jupiter: 490,000,000 miles from Sun; orbit about 12 Earth years; 1400× Earth's bulk; 17 moons total (including the stolen one).
- Jovian belts = dust.
- Jovians lower a rope with a grub. Grub falls and explodes, killing people.
- Mars: dying; canals; drying air. Ross's mock-scold ("you cannot insist").
- Mars welcome: four Earthians seized; electric capture.
- Trial at Maraban. Godfrey sentenced to life imprisonment; the three to death in three days.
- Plan: entering the ship, demonstration. Ross reduces gravity. Ship lifts three men and throws them out. One escapes down a rope; a soldier is caught.
- Dennis tortures captive with current. Captive later named Werran.
- Ship rescues Godfrey by lifting prison roofs. Battle: Martians vaporised. Regina floats them 3 ft above ground.

## Ch VII: The Story of a Star
- Light-beam ray from distant star shows history of an Earth-like world.
- Werran (Martian general) becomes ally; he never laughs.
- Jovian names: Gorok (Earth, "small"), Lazak (Mars, "ruby"), Milak (Jupiter, "beautiful garden"), Kulik (Sun, "learned").
- Jovian "Noah's Ark" animals offered; Godfrey refuses.
- First Martian laugh.
- Forgotten address; found at Kulametik, beside crater like flat cross.
- Beast from Carakulak: spinal gas kills within 50 ft.
- Month stay. Werran returned to Mars; Regina leaves him a red-light cup over his house.

## Ch VIII: A Jovian Bug
- Lab in Dennis's house. Insect called "Gorokakak" ("small fire-eater").
- Life history: winged parents, eleven parthenogenetic generations, mica-like cocoon.
- Net woven in a windowless building; test with phosphorus at over 3000°C.
- Two years of secrecy. Covered passage.
- Gilbert kidnapped by noose from airship; mechanics spared; pirate ship destroyed.
- Announcement: "The *Regina* will sail within ten days into the Sun."

## Ch IX: Testing the Web
- Public outcry; Government impotent.
- Twenty scientists invited. Water-cord "City of Earth" (Antistes footnote: *The Immortal Light*).
- Workmen fêted and then dropped.
- Net demonstration: explosives and phosphorus fail to ignite.
- Dennis's idea: fly fast through atmosphere. Round Earth twice at 20 miles.
- Departure for the Sun.

## Ch X: The Conspiracy
- Stars seen in all directions. Mira Ceti explained.
- Dissension: Edgar Holt leads eight objectors (incl. Bosworth Keeth).
- Gilbert records their plans via sehen-microphone.
- Mutineers locked in cabins; dumped on a purple-glowing planet near Venus.
- Dennis prays before descent.
- Sun: diameter 866,500 miles. Corona. Scientists: Crawford Rollsborough (chief astronomer), Price Rowland (physicist), Raymond Sorrel (geologist), Merrick Rutherford (metallurgist), Kirkby Reeve (zoologist).
- Ross controls gravity.

## Ch XI: "The Impregnable Rock"
- Godfrey and Sorrel debate Bible vs science.
- Sorrel's creation sequence: azoic rocks; Cambrian; Devonian; Carboniferous; Reptile Age; Tertiary; man last.
- Sun younger than Earth. Bullet experiment (coalescence).
- Nitrogen withdrawal would ignite world.
- Explosion in laboratory.

## Ch XII: Through Fire and Flame and Mystery
- Gilbert's steel box shatters. Dust everywhere.
- Corona cloud description. Photosphere = sea of fire.
- Ross reassures. Tidal "wave" of fire passes.
- Sunspots: "umbra", "penumbra", "nucleus".
- Sun: circumference 2,742,937 miles; diameter about 873,105 miles; rotation 6570 mph; surface gravity 28.75 (Earth=1).
- Descent: Field doubts; Godfrey's joke. Ship sinks into sun; sudden darkness.

## Ch XIII: "Vaults of Purple"
- Interior: pure nitrogen. Dust fallen. Sorrel: "Let us fall."
- Oxygen increasing. Dennis sleeps; Ross tells all to rest.
- Gilbert finds sound; explanation via interference.
- Rollsborough: light and sound parallels.
- Chaotic rock world with will-o'-the-wisp lights.
- Godfrey: "clouds with light on them."
- Earth-like atmosphere; golden insects with green elytra.
- Fiji Islands 2316 eruption reference.

## Ch XIV: Between Two Worlds
- Inner sun-sea: avalanche waves; meditation on injustice.
- Hairy hallucinations; "nebulous beings". Kelman, Ingle, Rutherford ("angels").
- Sorrel's theory: sun formed by planetary impact.
- Health fails; return journey.

## Ch XV: *Joci Causâ*
- Ross: "must find mutineers." Venus-satellite vanished.
- Godfrey's jokes (Jupiter "grub" address).
- Wave to Earth: Earth's answer on satellite's whereabouts.
- Riding horse-like animals across water; Kelman falls; Ingle injured; Dick the terrier.
- Telepathy fails outside solar system.
- Natives: hairy, sexless, unclothed, draw food from air.
- Dennis/Ross/Gilbert propose drawing the runaway planet back; Rollsborough and Sorrel object; eleven men vote in favour.

## Ch XVI: "A Race of Laughing Philosophers"
- Eight mutineers dropped on the planet (natives call Sun "Claytor", Mercury "Celtas", their world "Ramsar", Surans, Venus "Lovis", Earth "Rathela").
- Mutineers: Edgar Holt (leader), Bosworth Keeth (chemist), Fred Congreve (electrician), Pease Dawson, Ellis Siddall (the reformer), Herbert Wadsworth, Brookes Hewitt, Aubrey Bolford (astronomer).
- They corrupt natives with alcohol, smoking, gambling and shells. Pauperism, theft, crime.
- Climate collapses; electric storm; cave refuge. Dawson near death; Bible-millstone speech.
- Rain; cave exit. Regina seen as a comet.

## Ch XVII: Small Profit and Quick Return
- Planet's drift; electrical "smell"; ozone air; natives suffer.
- Godfrey's speech urging mercy ("giant's strength"). Rollsborough and Sorrel advise.
- Dennis confesses. Planet returned to orbit.
- Mutineers rescued from cave; Ross explains the trick.
- Final wave: "In three days expect the REGINA!"
- Back matter: adverts for *The Immortal Light* and *The Stolen Planet*, with press quotes.
